chapter: The Original Dixieland band to California
title: The radio show and early New Orleans bands on radio
summary: The band was sold to radio under the Original Dixieland Jazz Band name; Joe recalls few early radio bands, Celestin among them.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Ah, there's one New Orleans musician I've never heard of.

But what got us, instead of Bespawn(?) and Hill putting in a transfer, like they're supposed to... In San Francisco, when you got there, before you hit one note, you put in your transfer. But we didn't do it. And we had a radio show to play. I'll never forget it. And Phil Harris was the emcee at the time on this radio station in San Francisco.
Let me ask perhaps a dumb question. But why did they put your band on the radio? What other bands were on radio shows at that time?

I don't know why they did it. This Bespawn(?) and Hill had sold them a bill of goods that he had a helluva good band from New Orleans. They advertised us as the Original Dixieland Jazz Band, you see. He misled a lot of people.
I'm trying to think who was the third band I ever heard of that played on the radio -- New Orleans band, I mean.
Not many of the New Orleans musicians talk about doing radio things.
I guess perhaps in the South they didn't have all that so much, but...
Well, Papa Celestin had a radio show at one time, a long time ago. And then the first band I really remember was Ory and Jimmie Noone and them, when Orson Welles had them.
Well, that was '44. I mean, there's fifteen years or so difference.
Well, before that I can't remember any.
There are a few of those bands that were...
Well, wait a minute, let's think. If you're talking about '27, '28... Well, no, the Depression wasn't around then yet, was it, so...
Yeah, it would seem so. And from Oakland you went up to Seattle first, or...
